full_text_en:
Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. v. Zhejiang Huatian Industry Co., Ltd., Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over trademark infringement

【Ruling Summary】

1. Pursuant to Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Jurisdiction and Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Cases, where a lawsuit is filed for infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark that occurred before the implementation of the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law, and the people's court has not yet rendered a final judgment at the time of such implementation, the case shall be handled by reference to Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law.

2. Pursuant to Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks, when a people's court determines the amount of compensation for damages to be paid by the infringer in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 56 of the Trademark Law, it may calculate the amount of compensation based on the method of calculation chosen by the right holder.

3. In calculating the illegal gains of a trademark infringer, reference may be made to the provisions of the third paragraph of Article 20 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases, i.e., the profits derived by the infringer from the infringement shall generally be calculated on the basis of the infringer's operating profit; for an infringer who is entirely engaged in infringement, the profit may be calculated on the basis of sales profit.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min San Zhong Zi No. 1

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Zhejiang Huatian Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jili Avenue, Lu'nan, Luqiao District, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Wang Xian'gen, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Bo, lawyer of Beijing Hongfan Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., domiciled at 2500 Shinkai, Iwata City, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan.

Legal Representative: Takashi Kajikawa, President of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ji Jun, lawyer of Beijing Shize Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hua Lei, lawyer of Beijing Shize Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Nanjing Lianrun Automobile and Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd., domiciled at 47-6 Huju South Road, Jianye District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Xu Hanlin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Bing, lawyer of Nanjing Zhongsheng Law Firm, Jiangsu Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Lin, lawyer of Nanjing Zhongsheng Law Firm, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant at First Instance: Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jichang Road, Lu'nan, Luqiao District, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xinmin, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Taizhou Jiaji Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 7, Jili Avenue Living Quarters, Jichang Road, Luqiao, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Zhijun, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

The Appellant Zhejiang Huatian Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhejiang Huatian Company) appealed to this Court against the Civil Judgment (2002) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 006 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court in the case of dispute over trademark infringement with the Respondent Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. and the Defendants at First Instance Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taizhou Huatian Sales Company), Taizhou Jiaji Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taizhou Jiaji Company), and Nanjing Lianrun Automobile and Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nanjing Lianrun Company). After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Kong Xiangjun, Deputy Chief Judge of the Third Civil Adjudication Tribunal, serving as Presiding Judge, Acting Judges Xia Junli and Wang Yanfang as members, with Court Clerks Bao Shuo and Cui Lina serving as court recorders, and held a public hearing in this case. Xu Bo, agent ad litem of Zhejiang Huatian Company, Ji Jun and Hua Lei, agents ad litem of Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., and Sun Bing and Zhu Lin, agents ad litem of Nanjing Lianrun Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company, after being duly summoned by summons served by this Court, failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons. This Court has tried the case by default. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial: The registered trademarks "YAMAHA", "雅马哈" (Yamaha), and "FUTURE" were lawfully registered in China by Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. of Japan, with Registration Nos. 1255404, 1337138, and 33, respectively. The trademarks "YAMAHA" and "雅马哈" are approved for use on various means of transportation and their parts in Class 12, including motorcycles, automobiles, bicycles, engines for land vehicles, motorcycle parts and accessories, and motorcycle fuel tanks. The trademark "FUTURE" is approved for use on goods such as motorcycles and their parts, ships and their parts, aircraft and their parts, etc., also in Class 12.

In April 1999, the plaintiff's registered trademarks "雅马哈" and "YAMAHA" were included in the National Catalogue of Key Trademarks Protected by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce.

On July 31, 2001, the Taizhou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce rendered an administrative penalty decision against Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, finding that from December 2000 to February 2001, Zhejiang Huatian Company had produced a total of 534 motorcycles bearing the characters "华田摩托·日本YAMAHA株式会社" words, among which 379 motorcycles had "FUTURE" stickers affixed to both sides of the rear trim panels. The models included HT50QT-12 Fengfan, HT150T-10 Shayu Wang, HT125T-5 Xinxunfeng, HT150T-11 Feijian, HT150T-9 Shenxing Taibao, HT250T Shenxing Taibao, HT125-2A Wang Taizi, and HT100-5 Wanliang, with a total business volume of RMB 3,263,486.09. Of the 534 motorcycles produced, 338 were sold by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, with total sales revenue of RMB 2,136,273.09. The Taizhou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce found that the above conduct of the two companies infringed the plaintiff's trademark rights and imposed penalties on them. This penalty decision was upheld upon administrative reconsideration by the Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce and was subsequently affirmed by the administrative judgment of the Jiaojiang District People's Court of Taizhou City.

A set of photographs taken by the industry and commerce authority before the investigation of Zhejiang Huatian Company showed that the prominently displayed positions in the operation and maintenance manual for Huatian brand HT125T-5 motorcycles bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." On the product packaging boxes, the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." were prominently marked in the center in large font, and below them, in relatively smaller font, the name of the co-manufacturer, "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Co., Ltd.," was marked. Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Co., Ltd. changed its name to Zhejiang Huatian Company on January 19, 2001.

On April 16, 2001, the Nanjing Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a penalty decision against Nanjing Lianrun Company, finding that around the time of the Spring Festival in 2001, the company had purchased 122 Huatian brand YAMAHA motorcycles from Zhejiang Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Company, valued at RMB 470,000. The outer packaging of these motorcycles bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.," and the motorcycle bodies bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "FUTURE." The authority found that the company's above conduct constituted trademark infringement and imposed administrative penalties. On March 21, 2001, Taizhou Yamaha Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. sent a letter to Nanjing Lianrun Company requesting the return of the 122 motorcycles dispatched to Nanjing Lianrun Company. On April 9, 2001, Taizhou Yamaha Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. changed its name to Taizhou Huatian Sales Company. On April 22, 2001, Taizhou Huatian Sales Company issued a receipt to Nanjing Lianrun Company, acknowledging the return of 122 Huatian brand motorcycles.

Furthermore, on November 27, 2000, Changxing Jinying Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. purchased 11 Huatian brand motorcycles from Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, involving models HT125T-5 (purchase price RMB 7,370), HT150T-10 (purchase price RMB 8,220), and HT150T-9 (purchase price RMB 8,920). From November 2000 to March 27, 2001, Deqing County Shuangfa Motorcycle Co., Ltd. of Zhejiang Province purchased 30 Huatian brand motorcycles from Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, involving models HT125T-5 (purchase price RMB 7,680), HT150T-9 (two at purchase price RMB 9,280 and two at RMB 8,480), HT150T-10 (purchase price RMB 7,780), HT150T-11 (purchase price RMB 8,780), HT50QT-12 (purchase price RMB 6,880), HT125-2A (purchase price RMB 10,980), and HT250T (purchase price RMB 12,480). The light boxes, exhaust pipes, and shock absorbers of these two batches of motorcycles all bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." Additionally, six Huatang brand motorcycles displayed in the showroom of Shuangfa Motorcycle Co., Ltd. not only bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." but also the word "FUTURE" on the side covers. The above facts were confirmed by the penalty decisions of the Changxing County and Deqing County Administrations for Industry and Commerce, which also found that these products were manufactured by Zhejiang Jiaji Company.

In Issue 95 of Motorcycle Business Information on December 12, 2000, a "Solemn Statement" signed by "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. and Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Co., Ltd." was published. This statement, in response to a previous "Strict Statement" made by the plaintiff in newspapers to clarify consumers' misunderstandings and crack down on infringement, claimed that the content of the plaintiff's statement was untrue and indicated that they might seek legal resolution. Additionally, in Issue 663 of Motorcycle Business Information on January 2, 2001, an advertisement for the HT125T-5 Xinxunfeng motorcycle used the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. Huatian Motorcycle," and the motorcycle shock absorbers bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." The page was signed by "Taizhou Yamaha Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd.," and its address, contact telephone number, and fax number were identical to those of Zhejiang Huatian Company in Issue 702 on May 29, 2001.

During the trial of this case, the court of first instance, upon the plaintiff's application, issued a ruling on June 27, 2003, to preserve eight accounting records books of Zhejiang Huatian Company. On January 12, 2004, upon the plaintiff's application, it commissioned an auditing institution to conduct a judicial audit of the sealed accounting records to determine the profits from Zhejiang Huatian Company's production and sale of the motorcycles involved. On February 12, 2004, the auditing institution sent a letter to the court of first instance stating that the financial materials for the separate audit of the eight types of motorcycles involved were incomplete and listed 13 types of materials needed. In response, the court of first instance organized both parties to cross-examine the sealed accounting records and set a deadline for the defendants Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company to provide the required financial materials. Zhejiang Huatian Company refused to provide them within the deadline. Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, citing the company's long history, the impossibility of maintaining standardized financial records, and the company's restructuring, failed to provide the relevant audit materials. Moreover, during the court hearing of the first instance, it clearly stated that it would not provide financial materials on sales costs or business registration materials reflecting its operating status.

On August 22, 2004, based on the available materials, the auditing institution issued an audit report stating: from December 2000 to March 2001, Zhejiang Huatian Company produced and sold 2,113 motorcycles of the eight models involved. "Based on the accounting vouchers of Huatian Company (Note: Zhejiang Huatian Company), the sales profit of the eight types of motorcycles produced by Huatian Company was RMB -37,921.49, the operating profit was RMB -152,195.84, and the total profit was RMB -152,195.84... Zhejiang Huatian Company sold a total of 2,094 motorcycles of the audited models to Taizhou Jiaji Company, with sales revenue of RMB 8,403,495.76, product sales profit of RMB -30,106.16, operating profit of RMB -143,522.27, and total profit of RMB -143,522.27."

Meanwhile, during the trial of the first instance, upon the plaintiff's application, the court of first instance ordered evidence preservation against defendant Taizhou Jiaji Company. After being unable to execute the preservation measures due to other reasons, it required the company to submit evidence materials subject to the preservation order. The company and its legal representative, within the prescribed time limit, refused to provide the relevant evidence materials.

The court of first instance further found: On September 25, 2000, Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. changed its name from "Jiji Equipment Co., Ltd.," and Li Shutong served as a director and chairman of the board of the company.

On January 1, 2001, Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd., represented by Takashi Nakade, and Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Co., Ltd., represented by Jiang Fuchun, signed the "Agreement on Technical Cooperation, Enterprise Management, and Use of Trade Name," Article 5 of which provided: "(Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.) agrees that Party B (Taizhou Huatian Motorcycle Co., Ltd.) may use the trade name 'Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.' approved by the Japanese Local Legal Affairs Bureau and its Chinese counterpart 'Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.' within the following scope: (1) on Huatian motorcycle and engine products and advertising and promotional materials; (2) used by Taizhou Yamaha Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd.; (3) used by Huatian brand motorcycle dealers and in-store interior decoration."

On January 24, 2001, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Komatsu Branch of the Kanazawa District Court in Japan, arguing that Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.'s registration of that trade name and its use in its business was likely to cause confusion and misidentification, harming the plaintiff's business interests in China and Japan. On September 12, 2001, the Komatsu Branch of the Kanazawa District Court, given the defendant's failure to appear and submit a statement of defense, ruled in favor of the plaintiff's claim.

Regarding the establishment and changes of the relevant companies, the court of first instance also found:

On July 7, 1997, Zhejiang Jiaji Company was established. As of May 10, 2000, the company's legal representative was Li Shutong. Before May 26, 2002, Li Shutong was the largest shareholder.

On July 14, 1997, defendant Taizhou Jiaji Company was established, with legal representative Li Shutong. On April 9, 2001, Zhejiang Jiaji Company transferred all its equity in Taizhou Jiaji Company to Zhejiang Huatian Company.

From January 19 to July 23, 2001, Li Shutong served as the legal representative of Zhejiang Huatian Company.

The court of first instance held: The period of alleged infringement by the plaintiff against the defendants was from December 2000 to March 2001. According to Articles 8 and 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Jurisdiction and Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Cases, this case shall apply the pre-amendment Trademark Law and its Implementing Rules and other corresponding legal provisions. Regarding the determination of the amount of damages and the assumption of liability, reference may be made to Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law and the relevant judicial interpretations for handling.

Defendant Zhejiang Huatian Company used the plaintiff's registered trademark "FUTURE" on the motorcycles it produced and sold them. According to item (1) of the first paragraph of Article 38 of the pre-amendment Trademark Law, "Using a trademark identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the permission of the registrant" constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. The conduct of Zhejiang Huatian Company infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

Zhejiang Huatian Company's use of the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." on the motorcycles it produced and sold also infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. Reasons: 1. "YAMAHA" and "Yamaha" brand motorcycles were produced and sold domestically long before 2000. The plaintiff's registered trademarks are highly distinctive and well-known, and are familiar to the relevant public. 2. "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." has never been registered as a trade name or trademark in either Japan or China. Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. of Japan does not enjoy any trade name or trademark rights and is not entitled to license the use of "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." as a trade name to Zhejiang Huatian Company or Taizhou Huatian Sales Company. "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." was found to be illegally registered by a Japanese court, which ordered the cancellation of its registration and prohibited its use. Furthermore, any signs licensed for use by others must not conflict with prior rights protected by law and must not cause misunderstanding or confusion among the relevant public. The license granted by Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. to the defendants to use the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." on their produced and sold motorcycles and their packaging, or in other business operations, would inevitably cause the relevant public to misunderstand or be confused about the source of the products and business activities of the plaintiff and defendants, potentially leading them to mistakenly believe there is a special relationship between the plaintiff and defendants, thereby usurping the plaintiff's trademark interests and other business benefits derived therefrom, and disrupting market order. 3. Zhejiang Huatian Company's prominent use of the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "YAMAHA" is likely to cause misunderstanding and confusion among the relevant public. While the defendant indicated the manufacturer's corporate name in relevant positions on the product manual, certificate of quality, and outer packaging, it also prominently and conspicuously marked the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." in a larger font on various major parts of the motorcycles, their outer packaging, and manuals. The English word "YAMAHA" within this identifier is the most distinctive and recognizable element, easily attracting consumer attention. This constitutes prominent use of the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and has the practical effect of highlighting the "YAMAHA" mark, likely causing the relevant public to misunderstand, become confused, or draw erroneous associations regarding the plaintiff's well-known "YAMAHA" and "Yamaha" trademarks and operations, thereby infringing upon the plaintiff's trademark rights. 4. Zhejiang Huatian Company's use of these words was done with subjective malice to infringe the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. On January 1, 2001, when the original Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. entered into an agreement with the defendant Zhejiang Huatian Company, Li Shutong, who was a director and the chairman of the board of the former, was also the largest controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Huatian Company and soon became its chairman. As a long-term professional in the motorcycle industry, Li Shutong should have known that the plaintiff's "YAMAHA" and "Yamaha" trademarks were well-known in the industry. Yet, through the licensing agreement signed by Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. (where he was chairman) with Zhejiang Huatian Company, he allowed Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company to use the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." (Note: the original Chinese text uses both "日本YAMAHA株式会社" and "日本雅马哈株式会社" interchangeably; here both are translated as "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." for consistency, but the distinction should be noted if required). This shows a clear improper intent to infringe the plaintiff's trademark rights. According to Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Trademark Law before amendment, acts that "cause other damage to the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of another person" constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. Article 41, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the 1995 Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law stipulates that "using words or designs identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as a product name or product decoration on the same or similar goods, where such use is sufficient to cause misunderstanding" constitutes an infringing act under Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Trademark Law. The defendant's actions constitute infringement of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the "YAMAHA" and "Yamaha" registered trademarks.

According to Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "General Principles of Civil Law"), Zhejiang Huatian Company shall bear civil liability for ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses. Furthermore, Zhejiang Huatian Company's actions have, to a certain extent, harmed the plaintiff's business reputation. The "Solemn Declaration" it published in Motorcycle Business Information would clearly lead consumers to mistakenly believe who the true infringer is, also causing some damage to the plaintiff's business reputation. According to Article 120, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of Civil Law, it should issue an apology to the plaintiff in Motorcycle Business Information.

Defendant Taizhou Jiaji Company purchased more than 90% of the motorcycles produced by Zhejiang Huatian Company. There is no evidence, and it cannot be explained, that this was for its own consumption. It should be presumed that the company engaged in the above activities for business purposes, thus constituting a distribution of goods. Given that Li Shutong was simultaneously the legal representative of Zhejiang Huatian Company, Taizhou Jiaji Company, and Zhejiang Jiaji Company, and through absolute controlling stakes in Zhejiang Huatian Company and Zhejiang Jiaji Company, he held controlling interest in Taizhou Jiaji Company, with Zhejiang Huatian Company producing and Taizhou Jiaji Company selling the infringing products. Therefore, through this affiliated relationship and special controlling relationship, Taizhou Jiaji Company should have been aware that the products produced by Zhejiang Huatian Company infringed the plaintiff's trademark rights and that the goods it was distributing were infringing products. The advertisements published by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company in Motorcycle Business Information share exactly the same address, contact phone number, and fax number as those indicated by Zhejiang Huatian Company. There is a close affiliated relationship between the two defendants, operating as a single entity in their external business activities. Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and Zhejiang Huatian Company, as co-licensees of Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd., should also have been aware of the infringing mark "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." used by Zhejiang Huatian Company on the motorcycles it produced and sold. According to Article 38, Item (2) of the Trademark Law before amendment, "selling goods that one knows to be counterfeit registered trademark goods", and Item (4) "causing other damage to the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of another person" constitute infringement. Article 41, Item (1) of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law stipulates that "distributing goods that one knows or should know to be infringing upon the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of another person" constitutes an infringing act under Article 38, Item (4). Therefore, the actions of Taizhou Jiaji Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company in selling the involved motorcycles infringed the plaintiff's trademark rights.

Zhejiang Huatian Company produced the infringing products and sold them to Taizhou Jiaji Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, which then sold them externally. Zhejiang Huatian Company, Taizhou Jiaji Company, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company subjectively knew or should have known about the production, sale, and distribution process of the allegedly infringing products, and they jointly committed the infringing acts of production and sale. According to Article 130 of the General Principles of Civil Law: "Where two or more persons jointly commit an infringement that causes damage to another person, they shall bear joint and several liability." Taizhou Jiaji Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall bear joint tort liability with Zhejiang Huatian Company for their sales activities.

Nanjing Lianrun Company has returned all the motorcycles it purchased to Taizhou Huatian Sales Company, and there is no evidence proving it actually sold them externally. It has not yet constituted infringement upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark and shall not bear tort liability.

Regarding the determination of the number of infringing goods and the amount of damages: Because the financial information provided by Zhejiang Huatian Company was incomplete, and Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company are affiliated companies, it cannot be ruled out that they may have transferred profits. Therefore, the audit report's figures that Zhejiang Huatian Company produced and sold 2,113 motorcycles, sold 2,094 to Taizhou Jiaji Company, and sold 19 to Taizhou Huatian Sales Company are recognized, but the audit report's conclusion of loss is not accepted. According to general understanding and convention, products of the same model have the same appearance and bear the same markings. Although the defendants Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company claimed that not all 2,113 motorcycles were marked with "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.", they provided no evidence. Therefore, it is presumed that during the relatively short period in question, the main components of the 2,113 motorcycles of eight models produced and sold by Zhejiang Huatian Company all bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd.", and a considerable number of them had the word "FUTURE" affixed to both sides of the rear decorative panel. Zhejiang Huatian Company shall bear compensation liability for the 2,113 units; Taizhou Jiaji Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability for the 2,094 units; and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability for the 19 units.

Due to the incomplete financial information provided by Zhejiang Huatian Company to the court, the refusal of Taizhou Huatian Sales Company to provide relevant financial information reflecting its business status, and Taizhou Jiaji Company's two refusals to provide the financial information preserved by the court, as well as its refusal to attend the trial, according to Article 75 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings" which states, "If there is evidence to prove that a party possesses evidence but refuses to provide it without justifiable reasons, and the other party claims that the content of the evidence is adverse to the evidence holder, it may be presumed that the claim is established," it is presumed that the amount of compensation asserted and calculated by the plaintiff against Zhejiang Huatian Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company is established. Furthermore, the plaintiff's method of calculating the claimed damages has its reasonableness. According to Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law and Articles 13 and 14 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks," the plaintiff's choice to calculate damages based on the defendant's profits gained from the infringement has legal basis. Calculating the infringing profits of the producer and distributor as a whole has its reasonableness. The plaintiff's specific calculation method deducted the operating costs that could be calculated based on the available evidence. The plaintiff's method used, as much as possible, the cost, sales volume, and other relevant data from the audit report accepted by both parties. Although the administrative penalty decisions of Changxing County and Deqing County, Zhejiang Province identified the allegedly infringing products sold by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company as being produced by Zhejiang Jiaji Company, the model, appearance, and trademarks of these two batches of products are completely identical to the infringing products in this case and belong to the same category. The plaintiff's reference to the average market price of similar products sold by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company to calculate the sales price of the infringing goods in this case is not improper.

In summary, the court of first instance found that Zhejiang Huatian Company's production and sale, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company's and Taizhou Jiaji Company's sale of the involved motorcycles infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. The three defendants jointly committed the infringing acts with subjective joint intent and shall bear joint and several liability. Nanjing Lianrun Company's actions did not constitute trademark infringement and it shall not bear legal liability. Pursuant to Articles 118, 120, Paragraph 2, and 130 of the General Principles of Civil Law; Article 38, Paragraph 1, Items (1), (2), and (4) of the Trademark Law before amendment; Article 41, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (2) of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law before amendment; Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the amended Trademark Law; Articles 8 and 9 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Issues Concerning Jurisdiction and Scope of Legal Application in Trademark Cases"; Articles 13 and 14 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks"; and Article 75 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," the judgment was as follows: 1. Zhejiang Huatian Company, Taizhou Jiaji Company, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall immediately cease using the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "FUTURE" on their produced and sold motorcycles and parts, product manuals, certificates of quality, packaging boxes, etc., effective from the date the judgment takes legal effect. 2. Zhejiang Huatian Company, Taizhou Jiaji Company, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall publish an apology statement in Motorcycle Business Information apologizing to the plaintiff. 3. Zhejiang Huatian Company shall pay the plaintiff damages of RMB 8,300,440.43; Taizhou Jiaji Company shall bear joint and several liability for RMB 8,227,977.03 of that amount; and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall bear joint and several liability for RMB 72,463.4 of that amount. 4. The plaintiff's claim against Nanjing Lianrun Company is dismissed. Court acceptance fees, audit fees, and property preservation fees totaling RMB 133,779 shall be borne by Zhejiang Huatian Company in the amount of RMB 66,000, by Taizhou Jiaji Company in the amount of RMB 60,000, and by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company in the amount of RMB 7,779.

Zhejiang Huatian Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this court, arguing: (1) The appellant did not infringe the appellee's trademark rights. Reasons: (a) The appellant's use of "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." was based on the "Technical Cooperation, Enterprise Management, and Trade Name Use Agreement" entered into with Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. This agreement is legally valid and does not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations. (b) The "YAMAHA" trademark and "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." are marks with different wording. According to common practice and general understanding, the former is a trademark and the latter is a trade name; there is no possibility of causing public confusion or misunderstanding. The first instance court's finding has no basis. (c) The content of the advertisements and statement in Motorcycle Business Information was not done by the appellant. (2) The amount of compensation determined in the original judgment has no basis. Reasons: (a) The court partially accepted the audit conclusion while rejecting the loss conclusion, asserting that "the appellant may have transferred profits," which has no factual or legal basis. (b) The original determination that the number of infringing goods involved was 2,113 motorcycles has no factual basis. The appellee provided no evidence that all 2,113 units bore the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "FUTURE". The reasoning in the original judgment that "according to general understanding and convention, products of the same model have the same appearance and bear the same markings" is untenable. The infringing products should be the 534 units confirmed in the administrative penalty by the Taizhou Administration for Industry and Commerce. (c) The original court's use of the appellee's proposed calculation method to determine the compensation amount has no factual or legal basis. The sales price of a third party's products is not comparable to the present case, and determining the average sales price as over RMB 8,650 based on that is inconsistent with the facts. The appellee's proposed method did not deduct relevant costs, income tax, and other expenses. When the infringing profits cannot be calculated, the appellee should prove its own losses. If neither method can be applied, statutory compensation of not more than RMB 500,000 should apply. The appellant requests that this court reverse Items 1, 2, and 3 of the original judgment, dismiss the appellee's claims, and order the appellee to bear the litigation costs.

The appellee, Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., replied: (1) The first instance court's judgment that the appellant infringed trademark rights has clear factual findings and correct legal application. Reasons: (a) The "Technical Cooperation, Enterprise Management, and Trade Name Use Agreement" between the appellant and Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd. is invalid. (b) The first instance court correctly found that the appellant's prominent use of "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "YAMAHA" would easily cause misunderstanding and confusion among the relevant public. (2) The appellant's claim that the original court's determination of damages had no factual basis cannot be established. Reasons: (a) The original court correctly used the price of infringing products produced by a third party to determine the sales price in this case. The infringing products sold by the third party were of the same model, appearance, and trademark as the products in this case, and all were sold by Taizhou Huatian Company. (b) The sales volume of the infringing goods was 2,113 units as confirmed by the audit report, not 534 units. The appellant failed to prove that the remaining products did not have the same model, appearance, and trademarks. (c) The appellee's method of calculating the claimed damages is reasonable, and existing costs have been deducted. Since the appellant refused to provide financial information, the first instance court correctly presumed the appellee's claim to be established. (d) This case should not apply statutory compensation of not more than RMB 500,000. (3) The appellant bears the burden of proving that the content of the advertisements and statement in Motorcycle Business Information was not its doing. (4) Taizhou Huatian Sales Company should bear joint and several compensation liability for the full amount of RMB 8,300,440.43, not the RMB 72,463.4 determined by the first instance court. The appellee requests that this court dismiss the appeal; and if the original judgment is affirmed, also order Taizhou Huatian Sales Company to bear tort compensation of RMB 8,300,440.43.

The original defendant, Nanjing Lianrun Company, replied: At the time it was penalized by the Nanjing Administration for Industry and Commerce, the respondent had returned all 122 motorcycles it had purchased and did not actually sell any or obtain any profits. It had no intent to infringe and should not bear liability. The first instance court's determination of liability regarding the respondent was clear and the legal application was correct. It requests that Item 4 of the original judgment be upheld.

The original defendants, Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company, did not respond.

This court finds, upon further investigation, that the facts found by the first instance court are true.

This court further finds: On the front cover and rear box of some motorcycles produced by Zhejiang Huatian Company, the four Chinese characters "株式会社" (Kabushiki Kaisha / Co., Ltd.) were arranged in two lines, one above the other, with their overall height being the same as "日本YAMAHA", and the characters were in a smaller font with thinner strokes.

This court holds that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Zhejiang Huatian Company's actions constituted infringement of Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd.'s exclusive right to use its registered trademark, and if infringement is established, how the amount of damages should be determined.

(1) Determination of the Infringing Act in this Case

Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. is the holder of the registered trademarks "YAMAHA" and "FUTURE," and its exclusive right to use these registered trademarks is protected by law. The "YAMAHA" registered trademark has high distinctiveness and is well-known in the motorcycle-related market. The words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." affixed by Zhejiang Huatian Company on the allegedly infringing goods appear to be a trade name or corporate name, but it has not been registered in Japan or China. By creating the counterfeit trade name or corporate name "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and incorporating within it the well-known "YAMAHA" registered trademark of Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. in the motorcycle market, and by affixing it on the allegedly infringing motorcycle goods and prominently displaying the "Japan YAMAHA" part in a larger font, Zhejiang Huatian Company's actions clearly manifested an intent to mislead the relevant public into connecting the allegedly infringing goods with the "YAMAHA" registered trademark. Objectively, this was sufficient to cause confusion as to the source of the goods in the motorcycle-related market. It can be determined that the actions caused damage to the exclusive right to use the "YAMAHA" registered trademark. The first instance court correctly determined that Zhejiang Huatian Company's actions constituted trademark infringement under Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China before revision, and Article 41, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the 1995 Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law. Zhejiang Huatian Company's appeal ground that its use of "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." was based on an agreement, that the words constitute a trade name different from the "YAMAHA" registered trademark, and that there is no possibility of public confusion or misunderstanding, and therefore does not constitute infringement, cannot be sustained.

(2) Concerning the Determination of the Amount of Compensation

Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Jurisdiction and Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Cases provides that, for cases filed before the implementation of the amendments to the Trademark Law regarding acts of infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, if the people's court has not yet rendered a final judgment at the time of implementation, the matter shall be handled with reference to the provisions of Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law. It was not inappropriate for the court of first instance to determine the amount of compensation by reference to the provisions of Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law and the relevant judicial interpretation.

Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks provides that, when a people's court determines the liability for damages of the infringer in accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law, it may calculate the amount of damages based on the calculation method chosen by the right holder. Article 14 of that Interpretation provides that the profits gained from the infringement referred to in Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law may be calculated as the product of the volume of infringing goods sold multiplied by the unit profit of such goods; if the unit profit of the goods cannot be ascertained, it shall be calculated based on the unit profit of the goods bearing the registered trademark. Given that Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. chose to calculate the amount of compensation based on the profits gained by the three defendants from the infringement, and its calculation method treated the infringing activities of the manufacturer and sellers as a whole and deducted the operating costs that could be calculated based on the available evidence, this was reasonable, and this Court adopts it.

The period of infringement determined in the administrative penalty decision of the Zhejiang Provincial Taizhou City Administration for Industry and Commerce was from December 2000 to February 2001, which is one month shorter than the period from December 2000 to March 2001 stated in the audit report. During the proceedings in the court of first instance and in this Court, Zhejiang Huatian Company failed to provide relevant evidence that the products other than the 534 units did not bear the words "Japan YAMAHA Co., Ltd." and "FUTURE". The court of first instance did not err in finding that the number of infringing products produced and sold by Zhejiang Huatian Company was 2,113 units. The ground of appeal by Zhejiang Huatian Company that the number of infringing products should be determined as 534 units lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

According to the facts found by the court of first instance, although the products involved in the penalty decisions of the Changxing County and Deqing County Administrations for Industry and Commerce in Zhejiang Province were purchased by Changxing Jinying Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd. and Deqing County Shuangfa Motorcycle Co., Ltd. from Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and were produced by Zhejiang Jiaji Company, they were products of the same type, and their model numbers, appearances, and trademarks were identical to those of the infringing products in this case. The plaintiff at first instance did not err in calculating the sales price of the infringing products in this case by reference to the average market price of similar products sold by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company. Given that the appellant's intent to infringe was relatively obvious and that it failed to provide complete financial materials during the proceedings in the court of first instance and in this Court, the court of first instance did not err in presuming that the amount of compensation claimed by Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. was established. Because the unit profit of the infringing products and the profits gained from the infringement in this case can be ascertained, the appellate request by Zhejiang Huatian Company that the calculation method of multiplying the quantity of infringing products by the profit of the products bearing the registered trademark should apply, or that compensation should be limited to RMB 500,000 or less, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

The calculation of the illegal gains of an infringer generally involves sales profit, operating profit, and net profit. Paragraph 3 of Article 20 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases provides that the profits gained by an infringer from the infringement shall generally be calculated based on the infringer's operating profit; for infringers who are entirely engaged in infringement, the calculation may be based on sales profit. These provisions may be used as a reference when calculating related issues. In this case, Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. claimed compensation based on the profits gained from the infringement and calculated operating profit, not sales profit or net profit. It had deducted the relevant product sales tax and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses, and there was no need to deduct corporate income tax. Because Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company refused to submit evidence regarding operating profit and costs to the court of first instance and did not file an appeal with this Court, this Court does not support the ground of appeal by Zhejiang Huatian Company that the calculation method proposed by Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. did not deduct operating costs, income tax, and other expenses. During the proceedings in this Court, Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. argued in its defense that the motorcycles sold by Zhejiang Huatian Company to Taizhou Jiaji Company were ultimately sold to Taizhou Huatian Sales Company for resale to external parties, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company should bear joint and several liability for the compensation amount of RMB 8,300,440.43, rather than the amount of RMB 72,463.40 determined in the judgment of first instance. Given that Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. did not file an appeal on this issue and did not provide relevant evidence to the court of first instance or this Court, this Court does not make a determination on this matter.

In summary, this Court finds that: The production and sale by Zhejiang Huatian Company, and the sale by Taizhou Huatian Sales Company and Taizhou Jiaji Company, of the motorcycles involved in this case infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. The three companies jointly committed the infringing acts and had subjective joint intent to infringe; therefore, they shall bear joint and several liability for the infringement. Nanjing Lianrun Company did not constitute infringement and shall not bear legal liability. The court of first instance correctly found the facts and correctly applied the law. Pursuant to Article 118, Paragraph 2 of Article 120, and Article 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law; Items (1), (2), and (4) of Paragraph 1 of Article 38 of the Trademark Law before amendment; Items (1) and (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 41 of the Implementing Rules of the Trademark Law before amendment; Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law after amendment; Articles 8 and 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Jurisdiction and Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Cases; Articles 13 and 14 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks; and Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

The court costs of the first instance are RMB 51,756, the audit fee is RMB 40,000, and the property preservation fee is RMB 42,023, totaling RMB 133,779. Of this amount, Zhejiang Huatian Company shall bear RMB 66,000, Taizhou Jiaji Company shall bear RMB 60,000, and Taizhou Huatian Sales Company shall bear RMB 7,779.

The court costs of the second instance are RMB 51,756, to be borne by Zhejiang Huatian Company.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for the period of delay in payment shall be doubled in accordance with the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

This judgment is final.
